sources.entry: Wave Subs - Generates SRT/ASS subtitles from any video with local AI and auto-translates them, fully offline.

summary.one_liner: Wave Subs is a free, open-source desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows that generates SRT/ASS subtitles from videos using local Whisper speech recognition and local or cloud translation, without uploading the video.
summary.what_it_does: It takes a video, audio file, subtitle file, or whole folder and produces subtitles: it uses embedded text subtitle tracks if present, otherwise recognizes speech with whisper.cpp (Whisper Tiny through Large v3) with automatic language detection. Cue timing is aligned to speech using Silero VAD and loudness analysis, and hallucinated or music-only cues are removed. Lines are translated into 29 target languages with local Qwen3 models through llama.cpp, or with any OpenAI-compatible cloud API the user configures. An optional on-screen text mode reads and translates signs and captions using the operating system's OCR. The built-in editor offers video preview, a glossary for consistent names, and a per-file quality report, and batch processing handles whole seasons.
use_cases: generate subtitles for a movie or TV episode with no subtitles
translate subtitles into another language offline
batch subtitle a season of videos
transcribe speech in video or audio files
edit and time subtitle files with video preview
keep character names consistent across subtitle episodes
how_to_run: scoop bucket add wavesubs (Windows, Scoop; the README's command is malformed)
Download the DMG, ZIP, or Windows installer from the release page
Launch the app and download a recommended Whisper model from the Convert page
Drop in a video, subtitle file, or folder to start
notable: Fully local pipeline: recognition, alignment, translation, OCR and editing run on the machine, with no account or analytics
Recognition model table reports meaning retention by language, and recommends models by RAM
On-screen text (signs, captions, chat bubbles) is read from the picture and placed next to the dialogue translation
Glossary and a final pass that unifies spelling of recurring proper nouns across a season
Supports 18 external subtitle formats with automatic encoding detection
caveats: Intel Macs are not supported, and there are no Windows ARM64 builds
Windows recognition is CPU-only and much slower than Apple Silicon; on-screen text recognition is weaker on Windows
Local translation models up to 8B are unreliable on proper nouns; the glossary is the recommended fix
Windows installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run
keywords: subtitle my tv show without uploading
